hints.title: 2D Envelope Nesting Order Obstacle
hints.text: An envelope fits inside another only if both width and height are strictly smaller. How can sorting width ascending while sorting equal-width heights descending convert this 2D problem into a 1D increasing chain?

hints.title: Descending Height Tie-Breaking Invariant
hints.text: Sorting heights descending for equal widths guarantees that two envelopes with the same width cannot both be included in a strictly increasing sequence of heights.

hints.title: Patience Sorting LIS Extraction Procedure
hints.text: Sort envelopes with custom comparator: width ascending, and height descending when widths tie. Extract the heights array. Apply patience sorting bisection on heights to maintain the smallest tail of increasing subsequences in O(N log N) time. Return the length of the tails array.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(N log N); patience sorting on heights takes O(N log N).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: O(N^2) standard LIS times out on 10^5 envelopes.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of tails uses O(N) space to maintain increasing sequence candidates.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorting heights in reverse order for identical widths so equal widths never chain together.
